prompt: The schematic requires a 100 nF capacitor. Your parts list gives 0.1 µF; a prefix chart says one microfarad is one thousand nanofarads. What is the sensible next step?

options.text: Treat the capacitances as equal, then check voltage rating, dielectric and tolerance
options.explanation: Correct. The prefixes express the same nominal capacitance, but value alone does not establish a suitable replacement.

options.text: Reject it because different prefixes always mean different parts
options.explanation: Different units can express the same physical value.

options.text: Fit a 100 µF part because the number 100 matches
options.explanation: That ignores the prefix and selects a capacitance one thousand times larger.

options.text: Assume every 0.1 µF part is interchangeable
options.explanation: Equal capacitance does not guarantee suitable voltage rating or other characteristics.

workedExample: Read the unit as part of the value. One tenth of a thousand nanofarads is 100 nF, so the nominal capacitance matches. Then check the properties the value marking does not establish. The prefix chart is a lookup aid, not something you must memorise.
